subject: USAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB495 — "define signed numeric data items" - PicInfo.FloatItem synthesizes `Signed: true`, category Numeric, PICTURE-less (§13.16.3 SR8; a PICTURE with a float usage is refused COBOL1521); probe p13 stores and displays -1 in a FLOAT-SHORT. "held in a floating-point format suitable for the machine" - FLOAT-SHORT maps to .NET `float`, FLOAT-LONG and FLOAT-EXTENDED to `double` (PicInfo.ClrType), 4/8/8 bytes (probe p13). "The size and permitted range of values … is defined by the implementor" - A.3 item 22 makes the trio processor-dependent, support IS claimed, and docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 row 22 plus §7 item 207 carry the determination. THE TWO NESTING OBLIGATIONS are the only hard constraints and both hold: any float-short value is expressible as float-long (float widens to double exactly - probe p57 round-trips 16777216 through FLOAT-SHORT to FLOAT-LONG with no loss, and probe p13 shows 0.1f arriving as 0.10000000149011612, the exact binary32 value, not a truncation), and any float-long value is expressible as float-extended (probe p57: 12345678901234 through FLOAT-LONG to FLOAT-EXTENDED and back leaves delta 0; probe p13 carries double.MaxValue through). Mapping FLOAT-EXTENDED to `double` rather than a wider type satisfies the rule, which requires only a SUPERSET relation, never a strictly wider format. conformance:cases/13.18.60-USAGE/float_usage exercises all three usages with expectations computed from the arithmetic, and the COBOL-2002 introduction gate fires below 2002 (COBOL0900, probe p48). || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The two nesting obligations - the only hard constraints the rule imposes, since size and range are left to the implementor - do hold, and I re-measured them rather than taking the adjudicator's word: FLOAT-SHORT 0.1 arrives in a FLOAT-LONG as 0.10000000149011612 (the exact binary32 value widened, no loss), 16777216 round-trips, and FLOAT-LONG 12345678901234 and 1.0E300 both arrive in a FLOAT-EXTENDED unchanged; mapping FLOAT-EXTENDED to binary64 satisfies a SUPERSET obligation, which is all the rule asks. What fails is the rule's opening sentence - 'The usages float-short, float-long and float-extended DEFINE SIGNED NUMERIC DATA ITEMS that are held in a floating-point format' - for the declaration shape where the usage arrives from a group entry. SS13.18.60.4 GR1 makes a group-level USAGE clause apply to each elementary item in the group, and SS13.16.3 SR8 (cite-checked) names float-short / float-long / float-extended among the usages for which a PICTURE clause SHALL NOT be specified, so `01 GF USAGE FLOAT-LONG.  05 AL.` describes an elementary 8-byte floating-point item. MEASURED: AL has FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH 0 - a zero-length group, no diagnostic, exit 0 - so it is not a signed numeric data item at all and holds no floating-point value. The control in the same probe shows the compiler resolves the INDEX case correctly (`01 GI USAGE INDEX.  05 AI.` -> 8), and a second probe shows the SS13.18.60.3 SR2 explicit-on-both-entries form works (`05 AL USAGE FLOAT-BINARY-64.` -> 8), so the group USAGE clause is accepted and only the GR1 inheritance path is unimplemented for this family. A MOVE into such an item crashes the compiler outright (unhandled NullReferenceException in MoveEmitter.ConvertSource) rather than being diagnosed. NOTE FOR THE REGISTRAR: ONE shared root defect with my GR12, GR14, GR15 and GR21 verdicts - picture-less group-usage inheritance implemented for USAGE INDEX only; one fix closes all five. Also worth recording, though it does not by itself change the verdict: the cited test conformance:cases/13.18.60-USAGE/float_usage exercises the three usages but nothing in it pins the nesting obligations as such, so the rule's only hard requirement is measured here and nowhere in the suite. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/Model/PicInfo.cs#PicInfo.FloatItem; src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/Model/PicInfo.cs#PicInfo.ClrType; src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/PictureAnalyzer.cs#PictureAnalyzer.ParseUsage; docs/CONFORMANCE.md#DOC-A.1-207 || CLOSED 2026-09-09 by kb/Work PB495 (landed). The REFUTED paragraph above names the ONE root it shares with GR13, GR14, GR15 and GR21 -- "picture-less group-usage inheritance implemented for INDEX only" -- and says in terms that one fix closes all five. That fix is landed: 13.18.60.4 GR1 is now implemented as an EQUIVALENCE rather than as a special case, over ONE derivation of an elementary item's effective usage (its own USAGE clause, else the nearest enclosing one) feeding the group-header shed, the leaf's representation and every 13.18.60.3 screen through the same code the written-clause path runs. So `01 GB USAGE BINARY-SHORT. 05 AB.` is a 2-byte binary item and `01 GF USAGE FLOAT-LONG. 05 AL.` an 8-byte floating-point one, not the ZERO-LENGTH cells measured above, and the MOVE that crashed the compiler with an unhandled NullReferenceException in MoveEmitter.ConvertSource runs. RE-MEASURED, both spellings, whole matrix: a (usage x picture x arm) sweep of 138 cells found 108 DIFFERING on the pre-fix tree 39479e19 and 0 differing after, and the equivalence is now a drift theory over the whole Usage enum rather than a set of cases. The spec-derived witnesses are the two new goldens: conformance:cases/13.18.60-USAGE/pb495_group_usage_applies_to_each_leaf prints W=1 2 4 8 4 8 8 (binary-char/-short/-long/-double, float-short, float-long, index) with GRP=4 for a two-leaf BINARY-SHORT group and CTL=2 for the written-clause control, and conformance:cases/13.18.60-USAGE/pb495_group_usage_standard_float prints W=4 8 2 2 with F=16777216 16777217 -- 2**24+1 rounded by binary32 and held exactly by binary64, the sharpest single discriminator between the two interchange formats -- and N=-32768 65535, which is GR21 sentence 2's SIGNED/UNSIGNED length identity together with the UNSIGNED phrase reaching the leaf from the group entry. Everything the REFUTED paragraph credits as already holding is unchanged.
